events.objective: Establish the true symptom picture for the quote-latency incident: using query_metrics and query_logs, determine (1) the onset time of pricing-engine p99>2s and deadline-exceeded errors, (2) whether latency degradation is confined to pricing-engine or also visible in other services (trading screens/app, market-data, quote cache, gateways) over 2026-04-09 10:00-15:00Z, and (3) the error signatures in pricing-engine logs (timeouts vs 5xx vs slow downstream calls) plus resource trends (CPU, memory, GC, connection pools, request rate) for pricing-engine and its top call targets. Report exact timestamps, affected services, and whether the pattern looks like self-saturation vs dependency slowness.

Enumerate all changes and dependencies around this window: using get_deployments and get_config_changes, list every change across ALL services (not just pricing-engine) from 2026-04-08T00:00Z to 2026-04-09T14:59Z, with timestamps and capability/flag details — explicitly check whether anything changed at or before the reported onset (~13:30Z or earlier). Using get_service_dependencies, map pricing-engine's upstream/downstream dependencies and shared components, identifying which are shared with other latency-sensitive services. Also use search_historical_incidents for prior 'quote latency' / 'deadline-exceeded' incidents and their root causes.

Correlate the change timeline against the precise onset time found in task a: given the onset timestamp and affected-service set from task a, determine which specific deployment or config change best explains it (timing, blast radius matching the affected services, shared component touched). Explicitly evaluate whether any change to a service other than pricing-engine could have caused pricing-engine deadline-exceeded (e.g. traffic shift, shared DB/cache change, dependency latency), and estimate whether the evidence supports a fault in pricing-engine itself or elsewhere.

events.statement: pricing-engine p99 latency was flat at ~60ms through the 13:00 bucket, then jumped to avg 1216.56ms / max 2309.91ms in the 13:15 bucket and peaked at avg 2097.96ms (max 2238.06ms) in the 13:30 bucket, remaining elevated through 14:45 (avg 1191.68ms).
pricing-engine error_rate was stable at ~0.2% until the 13:00 bucket, then rose to avg 2.11% (max 4.37%) in the 13:15 bucket and held ~4.0-4.2% through 14:45.

All 192 pricing-engine ERROR logs 13:23:57Z-14:58:47Z share a single signature: 'quote computation deadline exceeded: market-data-service took <n>ms' (e.g. 5171ms, 8456ms) -- i.e. deadline exceeded on the downstream market-data-service call, not 5xx or local resource errors.

market-data-service shows nearly the same latency degradation as pricing-engine: p99 flat at ~40ms through 13:00, then avg 1037.16ms / max 1979.98ms at 13:15 and avg 1791.27ms at 13:30, tracking pricing-engine closely.

market-data-service CPU jumped from ~44.8% (13:00 bucket) to avg 69.65% / max 94.51% at 13:15 and avg 87.54% at 13:30, while pricing-engine CPU stayed flat at ~39-40% across the whole window (13:15=39.77%, 13:30=39.57%).

market-data-service WARN logs 13:22:25Z-14:58:22Z are dominated (289 of 290) by 'cache miss storm: quote:<n> not in redis-cache, rebuilding from exchange feed snapshot (<n>ms)', with rebuilds taking 1-8.7s (e.g. 6864ms, 8748ms) -- pointing at the redis-cache dependency.

events.answer: pricing-engine p99 latency jumped from a steady ~60ms to ~1.2-2.3s starting in the 13:15-13:30Z bucket, with deadline-exceeded errors beginning 13:23:57Z. The degradation is NOT confined to pricing-engine: market-data-service shows an almost identical p99 rise (40ms -> ~1.8s) and its CPU jumps from ~45% to ~88% at 13:15, while pricing-engine's own CPU/memory stay flat (~40%), and market-data-service logs a "cache miss storm" against redis-cache from 13:22:25Z. This pattern points to dependency slowness in market-data-service (and its cache dependency), not pricing-engine self-saturation.

pricing-engine dependency graph: outbound edges to market-data-service (http) and redis-cache (cache); inbound edge from order-service (http), with api-gateway → order-service upstream. market-data-service itself calls redis-cache (cache) and exchange-gateway (http). redis-cache is the only node with "shared":true (type redis, owner platform); all other nodes are shared:false.

redis-cache is a shared component sitting on the pricing-engine → market-data-service → exchange-gateway quote path, i.e. a neighbour (market-data-service) can degrade pricing-engine through that shared cache; the highest-scoring historical lead is HIST-107 'Cold cache storm after redis failover' (services redis-cache, market-data-service; symptoms 'cache miss storm','quote latency'; root_cause 'Redis primary failure promoted an empty replica', match_score 3).

Historical incidents are leads only: HIST-113 (2026-01-28) was pricing-engine 'quote timeouts'/'cpu 99%' caused by capacity saturation at market open, HIST-107 (2025-12-09) was redis/market-data cache-miss storm, and HIST-101 (2025-08-14) showed a same-day release caused latency — but in auth-service login (bcrypt 10->14 in v6.4.0, rolled back), a different service and symptom than this incident.

events.answer: Across all services between 2026-04-08T00:00Z and 2026-04-09T14:59Z there was exactly ONE deployment (auth-service v7.2.0, 2026-04-09T11:30:00Z, "Session cookie hardening"), fully confirmed after retrying the initially incomplete query, and ZERO config/flag changes — nothing was deployed to or changed at pricing-engine (or any trading-path service) at or before the ~13:30Z onset, so no code/config change explains the degradation. pricing-engine's dependency graph is: order-service → pricing-engine → market-data-service → exchange-gateway (HTTP), with redis-cache as the single SHARED component (owner platform) used by both pricing-engine and market-data-service. Prior 'quote latency' incidents point to redis-cache/market-data-service (cache-miss storm after failover) and pricing-engine capacity saturation, not to a release; auth-service v7.2.0 is a precedent for latency from a same-day release but is a different service and a different (login) symptom.

events.statement: No change of any kind touched the affected path or the shared component: redis-cache had 0 config changes (tc-017), market-data-service had 0 deployments (tc-018) and 0 config changes (tc-019) across 2026-04-08/09, matching the earlier all-services result of exactly one deployment (auth-service v7.2.0, 11:30Z) and 0 config changes. So the change timeline contains nothing at or near the ~13:15Z onset.

Timing mismatch rules out the single deployment as cause: dep-5604 auth-service v7.2.0 went live at 2026-04-09T11:30:00Z and was never rolled back ('status': 'live', rolled_back_at null), ~1h45m before pricing-engine latency jumped in the 13:15Z bucket and ~1h53m before the first deadline-exceeded error at 13:23:57Z. An auth/login-path cookie change (SameSite=strict) has no blast radius matching a quote-path latency event.

Blast radius of the latency matches market-data-service, not pricing-engine: market-data-service p99 rose ~40ms→avg 1791.27ms and its CPU 44.8%→avg 87.54% at 13:30 with max 94.51%, while pricing-engine CPU stayed flat at 39.77%/39.57% across the same buckets. pricing-engine shows no local saturation to explain its own 2s+ latencies.

The shared component architecture permits a neighbour to break pricing-engine: an independent depth-2 query on market-data-service returns the same shared node set -- redis-cache (type redis, owner platform, shared:true) called by both pricing-engine and market-data-service, plus market-data-service → exchange-gateway → external exchange-api (has_telemetry:false) and additional callers api-gateway and portfolio-service. So market-data-service is a fan-out dependency of at least four services while redis-cache is the single shared datastore.

The cache-miss/rebuild signature starts at 13:22:25Z against redis-cache, after the 13:15Z metric-bucket latency rise, and its rebuild timings (1-8.7s, e.g. 6864ms, 8748ms) exceed pricing-engine's own deadline budgets (errors cite market-data-service taking 5171ms, 8456ms) -- consistent with a degraded shared cache/rebuild path rather than pricing-engine compute.

Historical leads, treated as leads only: HIST-107 'Cold cache storm after redis failover' (redis-cache/market-data-service, match_score 3) matches this symptom pattern, while HIST-113 (pricing-engine 99% CPU) implies self-saturation that the flat ~40% pricing-engine CPU here does NOT show, and the same-day-release precedent HIST-101 is a different service/symptom (auth-service login, rolled back).

events.description: No telemetry for redis-cache internals: I did not retrieve redis-cache metrics (memory pressure, evictions, hit rate, connection count, replica/failover state), because that was outside my change-timeline scope and dependencies only report redis-cache as having telemetry generically. Unknown whether the cache is evicting, capped on memory, or recovering from a primary/replica event.

No telemetry for exchange-api (has_telemetry:false, vendor-owned) and I did not query exchange-gateway metrics, so an upstream exchange-feed slowdown that makes cache rebuilds slow cannot be excluded.

Change coverage outside the query windows is limited to 2026-04-08T00:00Z-2026-04-09T14:59Z; infrastructure-level changes (e.g. a redis node restart, eviction policy or memory limit applied by an out-of-band operator action) would not appear in get_deployments/get_config_changes.

events.answer: No deployment or config change explains the onset: across ALL services only one change exists in the window (auth-service v7.2.0, 11:30Z, "Session cookie hardening"), ~2h before the 13:15Z latency jump, with zero config/flag changes anywhere and zero changes to pricing-engine, market-data-service, redis-cache or any trading-path service. The evidence supports a fault OUTSIDE pricing-engine: market-data-service degrades in lockstep (p99 ~40ms→~1.8s at 13:15, CPU 45%→88%) against redis-cache (shared component), with a cache-miss/rebuild storm from 13:22:25Z, while pricing-engine's own CPU/memory stay flat (~40%) and all its 192 errors are 'quote computation deadline exceeded: market-data-service took <n>ms'.
